geo/horizons-3e.glb.name: Horizons 3e (Intelsat / SKY Perfect JSAT)
geo/horizons-3e.glb.illustration: Boeing’s deployed Horizons 3e artwork published by JSAT International and the supplied aft close-up
geo/horizons-3e.glb.note: Arianespace identifies a three-axis Boeing 702MP, 6,441 kg at launch, 18.5 kW at beginning of life, with C- and Ku-band payloads. GCAT estimates a 7 m length, 3.3 m width and 35 m deployed span. The four reflector backs, aft ring and bell, silver tiled side and solar contacts follow the Horizons 3e artwork. Local dimensions, concealed Earth-facing equipment and finishes are illustrative.

geo/intelsat-10-02.glb.name: Intelsat 10-02
geo/intelsat-10-02.glb.illustration: MEV-2's on-orbit image of Intelsat 10-02 and the deployed spacecraft artwork
geo/intelsat-10-02.glb.shape: Box + 2 solar wings + 2 lateral reflector assemblies
geo/intelsat-10-02.glb.note: GCAT estimates a 5.8 m length, 2.4 m width and 35 m deployed span. The asymmetric rounded reflector outlines, bracing and aft nozzle follow the MEV-2 flight photograph. Panel dimensions, finish and hidden hardware are illustrative.

geo/mev.glb.name: Mission Extension Vehicle (MEV-1 / MEV-2)
geo/mev.glb.illustration: the ILS MEV-1 launch rendering, Space Logistics cleanroom photography and the MEV team's imager paper
geo/mev.glb.shape: Box + 2 panel wings + capture probe and docking legs
geo/mev.glb.note: GCAT lists a 2.5 m width and estimates a 5 m length and 25 m deployed span for both flights. The launch rendering and cleanroom photograph guide the rectangular arrays, yokes, blankets, propulsion booms and docking face. Hardware dimensions, camera locations, finishes and docking pose are illustrative.

geo/astra-3b.glb.name: SES ASTRA 3B
geo/astra-3b.glb.note: Arianespace gives a 4.5 × 3.2 × 2.8 m body and a 39.8 m deployed span. The model places the 2.8 m axis along the solar drives. The four aft-mounted reflector sizes, hinge positions, tilt, panel divisions and finishes are estimates from Astrium artwork. The cropped outer wing flap is modeled by symmetry.

geo/ses-17.glb.name: SES-17
geo/ses-17.glb.illustration: Thales Alenia Space's deployed SES-17 artwork in the Arianespace launch kit and on Skybrokers
geo/ses-17.glb.shape: Box + 2 cross-shaped solar wings + 2 reflector banks
geo/ses-17.glb.note: SES gives a 46 m deployed solar wingspan. The 5 m by 3.5 m body envelope is an estimate from GCAT. Panel shapes, reflector sizes and boom positions follow the artwork. The partly hidden reflector bank is modeled by symmetry.

geo/ref-skynet-4250.glb.note: NASA specifies a 1.37 m diameter, a 0.81 m drum and 1.6 m overall height. The two solar belts and the proportions of the despun feed follow the spacecraft photographs.

geo/ref-spacebus-4000c3-28526.glb.name: Spacebus 4000C3 · AMC-12 (NSS-10)
geo/ref-spacebus-4000c3-28526.glb.note: ILS gives 4,974 kg at spacecraft separation and 72 C-band transponders on AMC-12. GCAT estimates a 5.5 by 2.5 m envelope and 38 m deployed span. The two cruciform wings and three white reflectors follow the Alcatel illustration. Small fittings and reflector angles are approximate.

SSL_1300.glb.note: Intelsat 20 has a published 32.4 m deployed span and 8.2 by 3.5 by 3.2 m launch envelope. The body proportions and reflector mounts are estimated from the launch drawing.

geo/geostar-two-side-and-deck.glb.name: GEOStar-2 · Intelsat 23
geo/geostar-two-side-and-deck.glb.note: Orbital gives four panels per wing, 2.5 by 2.7 m side reflectors and a 1.3 by 1.65 m deck reflector. Bus and arm proportions are approximate.

geo/geostar-new-dawn.glb.name: GEOStar-2 · Intelsat 28 / New Dawn
geo/geostar-new-dawn.glb.note: The west C-band reflector failed to deploy. Its folded angle is illustrative. The Ku-band reflector and both four-panel wings are deployed.

geo/ssl-1300-protostar.glb.name: SSL 1300 · ProtoStar I / Intelsat 25
geo/ssl-1300-protostar.glb.note: Arianespace gives 3.8 by 2.4 by 2.1 m and 31.1 m across the deployed panels. Reflectors follow the SSL illustration.

geo/spacebus-3000b3-galaxy.glb.name: Spacebus 3000B3 · Galaxy 17
geo/spacebus-3000b3-galaxy.glb.note: Arianespace gives 3.75 by 1.8 by 2.3 m and a 36.9 m deployed span. Reflector shapes and mounting angles follow the flight illustration.

geo/ssl-1300-galaxy-crosswing.glb.name: SSL 1300 · cruciform wings and three reflectors

geo/ssl-1300-galaxy-telstar.glb.name: SSL 1300 · straight wings and three reflectors

geo/ssl-1300-mobile-12m.glb.name: SSL 1300 · ICO G1 mobile relay
geo/ssl-1300-mobile-12m.glb.note: ULA specifies a 12 m deployable mesh reflector. Boom and panel proportions follow the spacecraft illustration.

geo/maxar-1300-tempo-instrument.glb.name: Maxar 1300 · TEMPO / Intelsat 40e
geo/maxar-1300-tempo-instrument.glb.illustration: Maxar deployed artwork archived by Gunter Dirk Krebs and flight hardware photographs published by NASA
geo/maxar-1300-tempo-instrument.glb.shape: Blanketed bus + 2 solar wings + paired reflector bank + lateral reflector + Earth-facing spectrometer
geo/maxar-1300-tempo-instrument.glb.note: GCAT estimates an 8 m by 6 m spacecraft envelope and a 26 m deployed span. The spectrometer envelope is 1.4 × 1.1 × 1.2 m. Bare-bus proportions, reflector sizes, supports and the solar wing angle are estimated from the artwork and flight photographs.

geo/maxar-1300-jupiter-3.glb.name: Maxar 1300 · Jupiter 3
geo/maxar-1300-jupiter-3.glb.note: Hughes gives a deployed solar span of 127 ft (38.71 m). The aperture and equipment layout is approximate.

geo/a2100-four-panel-dual.glb.name: A2100 · four-section wings and two reflectors

geo/a2100-amc-compact.glb.name: AMC-10 and AMC-11 (Anik F4)
geo/a2100-amc-compact.glb.illustration: Lockheed Martin's all-C-band A2100 family illustration
geo/a2100-amc-compact.glb.note: GCAT supplies the representative envelope for AMC-10 and AMC-11. SES identifies the two as twins. The compact paddles and dominant side reflector follow the illustrated C-band family.

geo/a2100-muos.glb.name: A2100 · MUOS dual mesh
geo/a2100-muos.glb.note: Two offset booms support 14 m and 5.4 m mesh apertures. Wing and bus proportions are representative.

geo/spacebus-4000c2-twin.glb.name: Spacebus 4000C2 · APSTAR-6
geo/spacebus-4000c2-twin.glb.shape: Box + 2 straight solar wings + reflector bank
geo/spacebus-4000c2-twin.glb.note: APT identifies APSTAR-6 as a 4000C2 carrying 38 C-band and 12 Ku-band transponders. GCAT estimates a 5.0 by 2.5 m envelope and 38 m span. The straight wings, white apertures and radiator arrangement follow the Alcatel illustration. Small fittings and reflector angles are approximate.

geo/amc-early-hybrid.glb.name: AMC-1, AMC-2 and AMC-3
geo/amc-early-hybrid.glb.illustration: Lockheed Martin's GE-1 hybrid C/Ku spacecraft illustration

geo/amc-short-cband.glb.name: AMC-7, AMC-8 and AMC-18
geo/amc-short-cband.glb.illustration: Lockheed Martin's GE-8 illustration and the AMC-18 launch kit
geo/amc-short-cband.glb.note: The Arianespace AMC-18 launch kit gives a 3.8 by 1.9 by 1.9 m launch envelope and a 14.65 m deployed span. It represents this short-wing C-band family. Reflector size and local fittings are estimated from the illustrations.

geo/amc-hybrid-ka-ku.glb.name: AMC-15 and AMC-16
geo/amc-hybrid-ka-ku.glb.illustration: Lockheed Martin's AMC-15 hybrid Ka/Ku spacecraft illustration

geo/amc-21-geostar.glb.name: AMC-21
geo/amc-21-geostar.glb.illustration: Orbital ATK's AMC-21 spacecraft data sheet
geo/amc-21-geostar.glb.note: Orbital ATK specifies two 2.3 m dual-grid shaped reflectors and four panels per solar wing. The bus and span use the GCAT AMC-21 envelope. The support struts and surface finishes are illustrative.

geo/ciel-2.glb.name: Spacebus 4000C4 · Ciel-2
geo/ciel-2.glb.shape: Box + 2 broad solar wings + reflector bank
geo/ciel-2.glb.note: Ciel-2 is the C4 flight shown in the Thales illustration. ILS gives 5,561 kg at spacecraft separation. GCAT gives a 7.1 by 3.0 m spacecraft envelope and an estimated 35 m span. The paired three-panel outer bays and antenna layout follow the illustration. Reflector sizes, mounts and surface finishes are approximate.
